faqs.q: What is the casual loading for social workers?
faqs.a: Casual social workers covered by the SCHADS award receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. For example, a casual Level 4 pay point 1 social worker would earn $58.38 per hour ($46.70 × 1.25). This loading is paid in lieu of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and personal leave.

faqs.q: How is super calculated on a social worker salary?
faqs.a: Super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the salary. For a full‑time social worker earning $92,307.20 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $11,076.86 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from the employee’s pay; it is an extra benefit.

faqs.q: What tax applies to a social worker salary?
faqs.a: For the 2026–27 financial year, resident tax rates apply: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. A 2% Medicare levy is also applied (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds are not yet confirmed). For a $92,307.20 salary, the estimated tax plus Medicare is approximately $19,497.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Social Worker Salary Under the SCHADS Award

If you are looking for a **social worker salary** in Australia, the most common industrial instrument is the *Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award 2010* (the SCHADS award). This award covers employees in social and community services, crisis accommodation, and home care. The Fair Work Commission updates the award rates each year following the Annual Wage Review. The latest rates, effective from the first full pay period on or after 1 December 2026, are published by the Fair Work Ombudsman in the official pay guide.

### How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Salary

To estimate an annual salary from an hourly rate, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For full‑time employees, the standard week is 38 hours under the National Employment Standards. For example, a social worker classified at Level 4 pay point 1 earns $46.70 per hour. Multiply by 38 hours and 52 weeks:

$46.70 × 38 × 52 = $92,307.20 per year

This calculation assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a useful starting point for comparing job offers or budgeting.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. Multiply the weekly rate by 2. For the same social worker, the weekly rate under the award is $1,774.74, so the fortnightly gross pay is $3,549.48.

### Distinguishing Minimum Wage, Award Rates, and Casual Loading

It is important to understand the different pay standards:

- **National Minimum Wage**: From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour ($1,004.90 per week for 38 hours) as set by the Fair Work Commission. This applies to award/agreement‑free employees.
- **Award rates**: The SCHADS award provides higher minimum rates for social workers. For example, Level 4 pay point 1 is $46.70 per hour, well above the national minimum wage.
- **Casual loading**: Casual employees receive an additional 25% on top of the base hourly rate. For a casual social worker at Level 4 pay point 1, the rate becomes $58.38 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave.

### Super Guarantee Paid on Top

Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% of ordinary earnings on top of the salary. For a full‑time social worker earning $92,307.20, the employer contributes an extra $11,076.86 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from the employee’s pay; it is an additional benefit.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15%
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30%
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37%
- $190,001+: 45%

A 2% Medicare levy applies. Because the 2026–27 Medicare levy reduction thresholds are not yet confirmed, we use the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. For a $92,307.20 salary, the estimated tax plus Medicare is approximately $19,497. This leaves a take‑home pay of about $72,810 per year.

### Using the Timesheet and Other Tools

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter a base hourly rate and optionally add 25% casual loading. It then calculates annual, fortnightly, weekly, and monthly figures, along with estimated tax and super. For more detailed award information, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). You can also explore [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) basics, [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) after deductions, and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) rules.

### Summary

A social worker under the SCHADS award at Level 4 pay point 1 earns $46.70 per hour, or $92,307.20 annually for a 38‑hour week. Fortnightly pay is $3,549.48. Casual employees receive $58.38 per hour. Super of 12% is paid on top, and tax plus Medicare reduces the gross amount. Always check the specific classification and pay point in the award, as actual pay may vary with experience, allowances, and penalty rates.
